messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD#INC-2026-0423 — metering.consumer_lag_high (SEV: P1). Consumer group 'metering-group' lag > 15m for multiple partitions. Runbook: https://redwood.runbooks/ingest-lag

pagerduty: Alert assigned to andrew_oncall (ack required). Escalation policy: 3m -> oncall-backup.

andrew_oncall: Acked. I'm on it — pulling offsets/lag now. Anyone seen customer impact yet? @lisa-finance? :eyes:

pagerduty: andrew_oncall acknowledged the incident at 10:03.

maya_billing: seeing token-count diffs for today vs yesterday for a handful of customers. Example: cust-A tokens expected 1.2M, seeing 1.05M. Not huge but invoice run is due in 30m.

matt_sre: running quick check on Kafka consumer offsets. Output snippet: ```
# kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --describe --group metering-group
TOPIC           PARTITION  CURRENT-OFFSET  LOG-END-OFFSET  LAG
metering-events 4          1284850         1295400         10550
metering-events 7          0               1250000         1250000
```
Looks like partition 7 consumer is stuck (lag ~1.25M). Getting repeated commit failures in the pod logs.

andrew_oncall: logs from metering-consumer-7: ```
2026-04-23T09:58:02Z ERROR commit failed: OffsetOutOfRangeException partition=7
2026-04-23T09:58:05Z WARN GC pause 620ms
2026-04-23T10:00:01Z ERROR heartbeat timeout, leaving group
```

ops-bot: Suggested remediation: restart consumer pod metering-consumer-7, scale replicas to 6, and run backlog backfill job.

andrew_oncall: doing a rolling restart of that consumer pod now. Command: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/metering-consumer -n prod --selector=instance=7`

matt_sre: also bumping consumer replicas to 6 to spread partitions: `kubectl scale deployment metering-consumer --replicas=6 -n prod`

lisa-finance: If token counts differ post-mitigation we need to hold invoice run until reconciliation or else risk incorrect billing. Please confirm whether we can still safely run for the majority of customers.

andrew_oncall: noted. I'll aim for reconciliation within 45m. If we can't, we'll gate the invoice job for affected customers. Which customers flagged? @maya_billing pls paste list.

maya_billing: pasted list (partial): cust-A, cust-D, cust-Q. totals down by 2-10%. Will share query IDs in a sec.

pagerduty: Escalation triggered: oncall-backup notified (3m elapsed). oncall-backup assigned.

oncall-backup: taking over for overlap — will verify consumer restarts and watch lag metrics. Ping me if handoff needed.

andrew_oncall: handoff to oncall-backup at 10:06. I left steps in thread and linked the runbook.

ops-bot: New consumer pods started. Logs show GC spikes on node ip-10-2-4-11 which had high memory pressure. Consider cordon/drain if repeated.

matt_sre: after scale & restart, partition lag for #7 started decreasing: ```
partition 7 lag: 1,250,000 -> 600,000 -> 120,000 -> 0 (approx 20m)
```

andrew_oncall: scoreboard: scaled to 6, rotated the bad node, restarted pods. Lag now at ~0 for all partitions. Token counts beginning to reconcile; running ad-hoc aggregation to verify.

maya_billing: re-run compare query shows cust-A now at 1.198M (expected 1.2M) — within tolerance. cust-D and cust-Q also reconciled. Looks like backfill is catching up.

lisa-finance: thanks. Given reconciliation, we can proceed with invoice runs but hold for any customers in the affected list until we confirm final counts. I'll patch the invoice job to exclude flagged customers for this run. :thumbsup:

sre-lead: root cause candidate: consumer stuck due to long GC pause on one JVM instance + uneven partition assignment after recent deploy, which led to offsets not being committed and backlog growth. Action items: 1) adjust jvm flags to reduce pause times, 2) add_partition_rebalance alert when single-consumer lag > 5m, 3) add automatic consumer rebalancer to prefer even distribution.

andrew_oncall: filing an incident ticket and starting a backfill safer job for any missed messages. Ticket: INC-2026-0423 (metering ingest lag) — I'll add timeline + mitigations.

matt_sre: running a targeted backfill from retained S3 spool for day=2026-04-23 to ensure any stray messages are reprocessed. Command used: `./tools/backfill --topic metering-events --date 2026-04-23 --partitions 7`

ops-bot: Backfill job submitted, job-id bf-1785-42. Estimated runtime 12m.

pagerduty: Incident status: acknowledged -> mitigation in progress -> partial resolution. No automatic close until postmortem.

lisa-finance: customer impact assessment: invoice generation for 3 customers delayed up to 35m. No overcharges detected. We'll send outbound note to those customers proactively. Who owns customer comms?

maya_billing: I'll draft a short note and loop in CS with list.

andrew_oncall: marking mitigation complete at 10:40. Consumer lag cleared; backfill completed without errors. Will wait 30m for stability then move to post-incident.

sre-lead: assign owners: matt_sre -> permanent fix (consumer JVM tune + deployment gating), maya_billing -> reconciliation checks + autoreconcile playbook, finance -> customer comms.

andrew_oncall: ack. Postmortem next steps: timeline, root cause analysis, RCA action items with owners and due dates. I'll start the doc.

oncall-backup: closing loop — observed stable metrics for 25m. No further alerts. Good job team. :sparkles:

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0423 transitioned to status: resolved (mitigated). Please run postmortem template: https://redwood.postmortems/template

lisa-finance: confirm whether we need a billing credit for affected customers? Finance suggests no credit necessary since eventual processing matched expected counts, but we'll be conservative and offer one-time credit if customers report trouble.

andrew_oncall: noted. Will include customer impact + recommended comms in the postmortem.

matt_sre: follow-ups: add GC monitoring to instance-level dashboards, add consumer partition skew alert, and ensure deploys include a quick smoke-check of partition distribution.

andrew_oncall: last check at 11:00: all clear. closing thread when postmortem linked. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
